evidence: Words judged: the end of his quote as it reads in CONTEXT.txt, “I’m not going to use spiritual mumbo jumbo to shush your cries and make you forgive before you're ready. We’re not moving into this wound for good, either.” (the draft is the second sentence), against SOURCE.txt “But I’m also not going to build our whole life around this wound forever.” READING IT COLD: it reads naturally in his casual register. “either” is correct additive-negative grammar after the first refusal and takes over from the old “But ... also”; “We’re” is the speaker plus the hurt part (his old line already said “our whole life”), and “this wound” points where the old “this wound” did, at the hurt the part carries (the paragraph above says injury and anger). It follows from the sentence before it and turns the paragraph’s own point (if we remain in the anger forever we let the injury dictate how we live) into a line he can say to the part. The draft appears once in CONTEXT.txt with the article’s curly apostrophe and closing quote mark, the first half of the quote is unchanged from SOURCE.txt, and the change is the one the_change describes. MEANING: kept at the level that counts. Forgiveness is still not forced before the part is ready (unchanged first half), and the wound is still not to become a permanent condition (“forever” becomes “for good”), both said to the hurt part in his voice. Three shifts, none blocking: the image goes from building a life around the wound to moving into it; “whole life” is no longer said outright (moving in for good implies it, and the paragraph above states the consequence); and the deciding voice goes from the adult’s “I” to a shared “we”. The card should show these so he can judge them. No claim, fact, name, source or first-person detail is added (C01 to C04 absent). TELLS: I went through T01 to T29 and C01 to C04 on the sentence in its paragraph. The one row I find still happening is T12, and it is justified: the thought-level pair (do not force forgiveness, do not stay in the wound) is still there, but it is his point and the section’s (the heading is Forgiveness without bypass and the paragraph above says both sides), and the draft adds no symmetry; the mirrored frame “I’m not going to ... But I’m also not going to ...” is gone, and the “But” with it. T20 and T29 absent: it is not a clever closer or a moral; without it the quote would give only half of what the section says, so it adds the second side; it is plain, with no aphorism; the paragraphs around it end on long sentences (the Jesus sentence, the long closing sentence of the next section), so there is no run of short landings. T14 absent: nothing reordered or moved, one clause replaced in place. T15 absent: the frame changes along with the words, so it is not a swap. T16 and T18 absent: no reveal, no flip. T26 absent: “wound” occurs once in the section and “for good” does not repeat the “forever” above. T27 absent. T06 and T08 absent: no generic abstraction and nothing explains the image afterwards (the writer’s ledger calls the old phrase abstract, but “build our whole life around” is also figurative, so that reasoning overstates; the rows are absent either way). C02 absent: no new referent problem. LINTER: B7 short landing at paragraph end: accepted as resolved. The flag is the draft itself (9 words after a 19-word sentence), but the context answers it: it is the second half of his own quote, in the position his closing line had, with nothing after it, and it adds a side rather than summarising. D9 follows the source order: accepted as resolved. One paragraph, one clause replaced in place, so following the line’s one point is by design; T13 and T09 come out absent (the section keeps his uneven sentences). I judged the text only and did not check the Pangram results quoted in the_change. Outside the change, noticed and not caused by it: the unchanged first half has a straight apostrophe in you're among curly ones, identical in SOURCE.txt.
